title: Automatic ereq control with a ceiling (ereqmax)
purpose: Exercises the automatic control of the empirical-potential amplitude `ereq` in the `epsr` engine of EPSR [@soper1996,@soper2005]: with `ereqstep` > 0 the program steps `ereq` after each run according to the trend of the quality factor in the `.erg` history, biased by `bias`, and bounded by `ereqmin`/`ereqmax` [@epsrmanual]. This is how users let EPSR raise the EP amplitude gradually instead of setting it by hand.
fortran: `epsr_standalone_rev3.f`: `lsparabola1` (trend line fitted to the `.erg` history), `ptgnsq` (EP refinement with the new amplitude)
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. The EP amplitude starts at `ereq` = 10 kJ/mol and is stepped in units of 1 kJ/mol with the default bias 2 and a ceiling `ereqmax` = 14.
inputs: Copy of EPSR-test with only the `.pcof` header changed: `ereqmax 14.00` and `ereqstep 1.000 1.000` (both 0 in EPSR-test).
verification: Six chained passes, each reading the `.pcof` and `.erg` written by the previous one, so every step decision is fed back. The control is active: the EP energy column of the six new `.erg` lines of the Fortran reference reads 10, 10, 11, 11, 11, 12 and the final `.pcof` has `ereq` = 12; the ceiling (14) is therefore checked but not reached in this run. The random numbers drawn by the step rule come from the same `ran1` stream, and all 27 output files are identical after every pass.
